lessons.title: Story Time: Jack and the Beanstalk
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss the growth theme in a well-known story.
success_criteria: I can say how the beanstalk grew.
I can say what the story teaches about growth.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict the story from the title.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read Jack and the Beanstalk, modelling discussion of the (exaggerated) growth theme.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss how the story's growth compares to real plant growth.
resources_needed: Jack and the Beanstalk story book
key_questions: How fast did the beanstalk grow in the story?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and comparison to real-world knowledge — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the story and discuss real growth rates.
lessons.home_link: Tell the story of Jack and the Beanstalk to your family.

lessons.title: Measuring Our Growing Plants
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and record plant growth over time.
success_criteria: I can measure my plant's height.
I can record the measurement.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the seeds planted in Week 25.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring a plant's height using cubes/a ruler and recording in a growth chart.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure their own growing plant (if available) or a provided plant, recording height.
key_questions: How tall is your plant now?
Has it grown since last time?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare growth rate to a partner's plant

lessons.assessment_notes: Record measurement and data recording over time — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Measure a plant at home if you have one.

lessons.title: Observing Our Plant's Growth
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and describe changes in a growing plant.
success_criteria: I can describe how my plant has changed.
I can say what helped it grow.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what plants need to grow from Week 25.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model observing and describing changes in a plant (new leaves, height, colour).
lessons.independent_task: Children observe their plant and record changes in a simple observation diary.
key_questions: What has changed about your plant?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational skill over time, a key working scientifically objective — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Check on a plant at home and note any changes.

lessons.title: Writing a Plant Diary Entry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a diary entry describing plant growth.
success_criteria: I can write what my plant looks like now.
I can write in the first person.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a diary entry describing plant growth.
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own plant diary entry (2-3 sentences).
key_questions: What does your plant look like today?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note diary writing and observational recording combined — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Write about a plant you're growing or have seen.

lessons.title: Counting in 2s, 5s, 10s Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in 2s, 5s and 10s using a seed/plant context.
success_criteria: I can count in 2s.
I can count in 5s or 10s.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting in multiples from Week 16.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting seeds/plant pots in 2s, 5s and 10s.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise counting seeds/pots in multiples, recording sequences.
key_questions: How many pots if we count in 10s?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting in multiples consolidation — evidence for MATHS.N1.

lessons.title: Do All Seeds Need the Same Things?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to plan and set up a simple comparative test for seed germination.
success_criteria: I can set up a fair test.
I can predict what will happen.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what plants need to grow.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model setting up a comparative test (e.g. one seed with water, one without) to test what seeds need.
lessons.independent_task: Children help set up and predict the outcome of a simple seed comparison test.
key_questions: What do you predict will happen?

differentiation.support: Adult supports set-up and simple prediction
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for predictions in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early fair testing skill — evidence for SCI.PLA, a key working scientifically objective.
lessons.plenary: Recap the test set up and predictions made.
lessons.home_link: Predict what would happen if a plant didn't get water.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Growing Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read growth-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read growth words.
I can read a sentence about growing.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending growth-themed words (e.g. 'seed', 'grow', 'shoot').
lessons.independent_task: Children read growth-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading growth words over the week.

lessons.title: Shapes of Leaves and Flowers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify 2D shapes within plant structures.
success_criteria: I can name a shape I see in a leaf/flower.
I can describe why it's that shape.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss shapes found in nature (round leaves, star-shaped flowers, oval petals).
lessons.independent_task: Children identify and record shapes seen in leaf/flower pictures.

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify multiple shapes and count petals/sides

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition applied to nature — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Look for shapes in leaves or flowers outside.

lessons.title: Checking Our Seed Test
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and record the results of a comparative test.
success_criteria: I can observe what happened to the seeds.
I can compare the results.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the seed test set up on Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model observing and recording results of the comparative seed test.
lessons.independent_task: Children observe and record the results of their seed test, comparing to predictions.
key_questions: What happened to the seed with water?
What happened to the one without?

differentiation.greater_depth: Draw conclusions about what seeds need

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observation and conclusion-drawing skill — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.plenary: Recap what the test showed about seed needs.
lessons.home_link: Check on any seeds or plants growing at home.

lessons.title: Presenting Our Plant Journey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their plant's growth journey clearly.
success_criteria: I can describe how my plant has grown.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap plant diary entries and observations.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of a growth journey.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their plant's growth journey to a small group, answering a question.

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and scientific reporting progress — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Present your plant's growth to your family.

lessons.title: Growth Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a plant growth context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a growth context (e.g. plant grows 2cm more each week).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve growth-themed word problems, showing working.
key_questions: How tall will it be after another week?
How much has it grown altogether?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a growth word problem for your family.

lessons.title: From Seed to Plant: Life Cycle Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence the life cycle of a flowering plant.
success_criteria: I can order the plant life cycle stages.
I can name each stage.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the plant's growth journey observed this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the plant life cycle (seed, seedling, mature plant, flower, seed again) using a diagram.
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence and label plant life cycle picture cards.
key_questions: What happens after a plant flowers?

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence and explain all stages independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note life cycle sequencing understanding, linking to the chicken life cycle in Week 25 — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.plenary: Recap the plant life cycle sequence.
lessons.home_link: Look up the life cycle of a plant you like.

lessons.title: Growing Plants Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about growing plants.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's growing plants learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about growing plants, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What does a seed need to grow?
Why did the seed without water not grow?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on plant growth facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Measuring, Counting, Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply measuring, counting, and shape skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can measure growth.
I can count in multiples.
I can identify shapes.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of measuring, counting in multiples, and shape identification.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 31 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N1/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue measuring plant growth over the weekend.

lessons.title: Growing Plants Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about growing plants.
success_criteria: I can name what a seed needs to grow.
I can sequence the plant life cycle.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering seed testing, growth observation, and the plant life cycle.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Growing Plants' display featuring their plant diaries.
key_questions: What have we learned about growing plants?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note plant growth and enquiry understanding progress across the topic — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's growing plants learning.
lessons.home_link: Keep looking after your plant at home if you have one.
